root_cause: The ANSI tokenizer regex re_ansi in rich/ansi.py only matched OSC (ESC ]...ESC \), the single-char escapes in [(@-Z\-_] and CSI (ESC [ ...). Fp private escapes ESC 0 to ESC ? (0x30-0x3F, e.g. ESC 7/ESC 8 cursor save/restore used by Alpine apk) were not matched, so Text.from_ansi kept them as plain text and they ended up in output (test shows '?x' instead of 'x').
best_solution: Add one alternative at the front of the verbose regex: `(?:\x1b[0-?])|`. It is non-capturing, so match.groups() is (None, None) and _ansi_tokenize takes the else branch, yielding an empty token: the sequence is consumed and emits nothing. It does not overlap the other alternatives because '[' (0x5B) and ']' (0x5D) are outside 0x30-0x3F. The existing class [(@-Z\-_] must stay unchanged, because the tokenizer has a special case `if sgr == "(": position = end + 1` that strips charset designators such as ESC ( B. An equally valid fix is to extend the class to [(0-?@-Z\-_]: sgr='0'..'?' is truthy, not '(', and does not end in 'm', so it is skipped too.
acceptable_alternatives: Extend the capturing class to [(0-?@-Z\-_], keeping the leading '('. Anything that deletes '(' from the class breaks test_decode_issue_2688.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_ansi.py::test_strip_private_escape_sequences, parametrized over each char in '0123456789:;<=>?': Text.from_ansi(f'\x1b{code}x') printed with Console(force_terminal=True) must capture exactly 'x\n'. The existing test_decode_issue_2688 cases (ESC ( B, ESC ( J charset escapes stripped) must still pass.
locating_signals: The statement says 'updates the ANSI parser' and gives the exact byte range \x1b0-\x1b?. grep for 'ansi' leads to rich/ansi.py, where the module-level re_ansi regex is the only parser. No function is named, but the file holds only one regex, so there is nowhere else to put the fix.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed in the Kaggle env (v4/v6/v7/v8 false), and every pod run hit the 110-call cap (about 210-230 s). v4 and v7 produced empty patches. v6 wrote only a new tests/repro_issue.py and never touched rich/ansi.py, so all 16 hidden cases failed ('?x' != 'x'). v8 changed the correct line but replaced the class [(@-Z\-_] with [0-?@-Z\-_], which dropped the '(' literal. The 16 new tests passed, but 4 existing test_decode_issue_2688 cases regressed (ESC ( B / ESC ( J were no longer stripped: '\x1b(JHallo' != 'Hallo'). Prepending 0-? while keeping '(' would have passed.
generalizable_lesson: When widening a regex character class, only add ranges and diff the old class against the new one character by character. Never retype the class, because it is easy to drop a literal (here '(') that downstream code depends on through an equality check. Before editing, grep for code that compares the captured group (e.g. `== "("`), then run the module's existing tests (tests/test_<module>.py) after the change. Also, a repro test on its own is not a fix: when the call budget is nearly used up, spend it on the one-line source change the statement describes.
